title: Chicken Saagwala
subtitle: Spiced chicken in a fresh spinach sauce
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs simmered in a lightly spiced sauce built on blended fresh spinach. The spinach goes in at the end to keep its colour vivid and its flavour clean.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian curry also known as palak chicken, common across British-Indian restaurant cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze for up to 2 months. The spinach sauce may darken slightly on reheating but the flavour holds well.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch easily. Cook in a wide, deep pan.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. Reheat gently over a low heat with a splash of water.

content.text: Chicken saagwala is a spinach-based curry with a clean, grassy sauce. Add the blended spinach at the very end and do not overcook it after that point. Overcooking turns the sauce grey and the flavour dull.

items.prepNote: finely chopped, seeds in or out to taste

content.text: Wilt the spinach in a dry hot pan for 2 minutes. Transfer to a blender and blend with 60ml cold water to a smooth puree. Set aside.
In the same pan, heat the oil over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 15 minutes until deep golden. Stir regularly.
Add the garlic, ginger, and green chilli. Fry for 2 minutes.
Add the turmeric, cumin, coriander, and half the garam masala. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes until the sauce thickens and oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add the chicken and salt. Stir to coat. Cook uncovered on a medium heat for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Pour in the spinach puree. Stir well. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes only. Stir in the remaining garam masala and the yoghurt if using. Serve straight away.

items.symptom: The spinach sauce has turned grey-green.
items.cause: The spinach was cooked for too long after being added.
items.fix: Add the spinach puree in the last 3 to 4 minutes only and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The yoghurt has curdled in the sauce.
items.cause: The sauce was too hot when the yoghurt went in.
items.fix: Remove the pan from the heat for 30 seconds before stirring in the yoghurt. Use full-fat yoghurt for best results.

items.cause: It was cooked at too high a heat for too long.
items.fix: Keep the heat at medium throughout and check at 12 minutes. Thighs are forgiving but do not push past 20 minutes of active cooking.
